text:
anya: Heads-up — p99 spiked ~120ms after yesterday's kernel-router change on mixtral-8k. Seeing a ton of small KV evictions and immediate re-prefetches on long-prefix requests. infra-bot posted deploy 1799998000.

sam: Any flamegraphs or raw profiles?

maria: grabbed a quick profile from the canary window. p50 stable, p99 jumped from ~210ms -> ~330ms for mixtral-8k under long-prefix load (avg prefix ~900 tokens). Flamegraph: https://perf/redwood/fg/abc123 :flame:

devon: my 2c: looks like the new split-kernel path + fp8-quantized KV combo is causing extra cache-line churn. split path disables async-prefetch in the current kernel router config for heads>=32.

anya: repro script so others can run locally: `python tools/repro_kv.py --model mixtral-8k --seq 8192 --prefix 900 --iters 1000 --batch 1`

sam: running it now. also paste of the router patch that landed:

```
{"kernel_router": {"prefer_split_kernels": true, "head_threshold": 16, "async_prefetch": false}}
```

maria: quick suggestion: try toggling `async_prefetch: true` and `prefer_split_kernels: false` for the canary route, and compare fp8 vs fp16 for the cached K/V. if p99 improves with merged kernels or fp16, that's a clear interaction.

devon: numbers from my short local:
- fp8-kv + split kernels: p99 340ms
- fp16-kv + split kernels: p99 220ms
- fp8-kv + merged kernels: p99 215ms
so it's not just fp8 precision — split kernels + quantized layout = bad cache locality and extra memcpy.

anya: that matches my hypothesis — merged kernel keeps a contiguous KV read path, fewer memory ops. split path adds reshuffles and turns small reads into multiple cache misses.

sam: proposed immediate plan:
1) revert `prefer_split_kernels` for mixtral canary routes
2) re-enable `async_prefetch` for long-prefix policy (prefix > 512)
3) introduce eviction hysteresis (min_age=2 + prefetch coalescing) to avoid thrashing
4) add perf counters: `kv_format` and `kernel_path` tags to per-request metrics

devon: I'll open a canary PR and add the repro to the perf-suite. Also adding a small metric `kv_cache_fill_rate` per model and `kv_eviction_count`.

infra-bot: deploy started: route mixtral-8k canary -> 5% traffic (deploy id dpl-1799998890)

anya: after canary revert + async_prefetch enabled, p99 dropped back to ~225ms on route samples. letting canary run for 2h to validate. :thumbsup:

maria: extra follow-up: check RoPE scaling impact — some models with nonstandard RoPE bases expose head-dim misalignments on split kernels which can exacerbate the misreads when KV is quantized. filing a ticket.

sam: created TRELLIS-423: "roper-scaling + split-kernel + fp8 => kv read misalignment" https://trellis/redwood/tickets/423

anya: tl;dr: don't enable split-kernels + fp8-kv for heads>=32 on Mixtral/Qwen until we add prefetch coalescing and eviction hysteresis. Policy router should consider `model, head_dim, kv_format` when picking kernel path.

devon: assigned follow-ups to @devon and @maria — I'll run a matrix: {model: [mixtral-8k, qwen-7b, llama-2-13b], head_dims: [16,32,64], kv_format: [fp8,fp16,quant8], kernel_path: [split,merged]} and log p50/p95/p99.

sam: thanks all — good catch, this would have been nasty at 100% traffic. Will monitor TRELLIS-423 and the canary metrics.
